entries.note: The pane is bound to one game session ID through tab movement and reconnection. Bottom-up RGBA is flipped into a bounded canvas buffer, retaining only the newest pending animation frame. Focus owns native input; blur and detach release held controls. Current coordinates assume logical and drawable dimensions coincide, as observed in the initial NOLF menu run. High-DPI and relative aiming across pane sizes remain qualification work.

Pointer capture keeps compatibility mouse-up events targeted at the canvas when a press ends outside it. Continue using mouse down/up for individual chorded buttons: pointerdown only fires when the first mouse button goes down. Normal implicit capture loss follows the last mouse-up, when the held-button set is empty, so it must not cancel a still-held movement key. Unexpected capture loss or cancellation releases all native controls. Release clears sidecar input ownership even if DOM focus stays on the canvas; the next key-down or pointer lock acquisition must claim that ownership again. Native SDL integration tests cover actual outside release, chorded buttons, forced established capture loss, keyboard reacquisition and pane blur.
